bearings.paper_claim: Self-reported Big Five correlate with LIWC categories at most |rho| .08-.14 (abstract p. 843). The 52 categories explain a mean R2 of 5.07 percent of self-report variance (narrow categories, k = 25 self-report samples, n = 83,243-84,084). About 87 percent of that n is Schwartz et al. 2013 (n = 72,809). Heterogeneity significant in 96 percent of cue-validity effects. Table 7 lists LIWC best-category average r = .10 (self) against Moreno et al. .27, HTTP .31, IBM-WPI .13 and human judges .12, all uncorrected.
bearings.paper_location: Abstract p. 843; Table 3 note p. 853; Table 4 p. 854; heterogeneity p. 857; Table 7 p. 859 with footnote 9
bearings.system_side: Code matches the description. Exemplar lists include swear = damn hell crap (big5_traits.py:100). Per-1000-word rates are at :220. Hand-set weights W are at :179-185, the SMOreg override at :186-189, and corpus z-scoring at :241-242. The stated held-out CV mean .350 and E .510 were not found in the brain topic or the fec tree. The brain topic records only C +0.348 held-out (round 2, 2026-07-08).
bearings.transfer_conditions: Paper samples are mostly informal English social media and student or general-population samples, LIWC 2001-2015. Congressional speech is formal and partly staff-written, and the paper shows formality attenuates markers. The system uses exemplar lists, not licensed LIWC dictionaries, so category equivalence is unverified. Table 7 values are post hoc best-category maxima and cannot rank methods.
bearings.verifier_note: Abstract, Table 4 and Table 3 figures match the text. Softened because Table 7 omits IBM-WPI at .13, which is above LIWC at .10, and the paper calls the best-category comparison post hoc. The CV .350 and E .510 figures and the claim that RKH convergence is method-inflated were not found in the brain topic or the repo, so they are unsupported as written.

bearings.paper_claim: Bivariate cue-validity effects (self-report, Table 3): Openness words over six letters rho .11; Conscientiousness negative emotion -.12, swear -.11, anger -.10; Agreeableness anger -.14, swear -.10, negative emotion -.10, positive emotion .10. Emotional Stability has no first-person singular validity effect at |rho| .10 or more. Cue utilization (observer): Emotional Stability first-person singular -.29.
bearings.system_side: Verified SMOreg weights: A anger -.0202 (json line 66), A swear -.0323 (:87), C anger -.0556 (:95), C swear -.0446 (:116), O sixltr +.0292 (:147). The paper agrees on these signs. Disagreements: ES first-person singular +.0094 (:43), ES negative emotion -.0002 (:51), and E positive emotion -.0339 (:20). The rel line citations were wrong for A anger (cited :43).
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper estimates are bivariate correlations. SMOreg weights are multivariate, so suppression can flip signs without error. The ES first-person comparison sets an observer-based paper effect against a model fit to other data, so it is not like-for-like. The flagged signs remain UNVERIFIED (DE-062) and are an audit lead only.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper values match Table 3 and pp. 852-853. The contradicts label is too strong: the paper does not test SMOreg, and the ES first-person comparison mixes observer utilization with a self-report-fit model. Weight values and signs match the json. Relation changed to qualifies.

bearings.paper_claim: Observer-rated (cue utilization, k = 5, n = 1,637, mostly zero-acquaintance raters) explained variance averages 38.52 percent against 5.07 percent for self-report cue validity. Largest observer |rho| .39 (Agreeableness swear) and .31 (Extraversion word count). Emotional Stability has the lowest observer R2 at 31.48 percent. The authors say valid or utilized cues are not the same as true personality.
bearings.paper_location: Results pp. 852-853; Table 4 p. 854; Discussion p. 857; Limitations p. 861
bearings.system_side: Senate panels are 129 insiders and 125 academics (brain topic line 52). The brain topic says E and A clear both panels, and O, C and N are one-panel association supported (line 58). The rel's per-panel splits (O academics only, N insiders only, C insider only) and the A-ES figures of about .44 and .21 halo do not appear in the brain topic. The cited file fec/big5_improvements_eval.py is not in the repo.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper observer samples are k = 5 with n = 1,637, nearly all zero-acquaintance. The Senate panels are informed insiders and experts, which the paper could not test. SOKA predicts the overt traits (E, A) would pass and ES would be weakest, which fits the brain topic. Panel convergence shows raters and text use the same cues, not trait accuracy.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper numbers match. Softened because the per-panel assignments and the A-ES .44 and .21 halo figures are not in the brain topic. Recheck them against the source files before any use.

bearings.paper_claim: Emotional Stability relates negatively to negative-emotion words (cue validity rho -.12, p. 853) and to first-person singular pronouns (cue utilization rho -.29). Emotional Stability carries 6 of the 20 kernel markers (p. 853). The Emotional Stability negative-emotion validity effect weakens with publication year (Table 6, b = .006). No positive-emotion effect for Emotional Stability is reported.
bearings.paper_location: Results p. 853; Table 3; Table 6 p. 856; Discussion p. 858
bearings.system_side: The anchor in emit_affective_n.py counts first-person pronouns, a hand-written negative-affect regex and a hand-written positive-affect regex in interview text of 800 or more words, then z-scores them. These are custom lexicons, not LIWC dictionaries, despite the LIWC framing. Since round 7b the anchor is convergent-validity only (r = +.24 per the rel). Genre-transfer values (.050, .161) were not checked here.
bearings.transfer_conditions: The paper supports the sign structure for Emotional Stability only, and it reports heterogeneity by mode and formality. An expected anchor size near .24 is the analyst's inference, not a paper result. This is direction support only, not evidence that N predicts yielding.
bearings.verifier_note: Paper values match. Softened because the anchor uses custom regexes, not LIWC, and the paper has no Emotional Stability positive-emotion effect, so the 'less posemo' part of the support is not backed by the paper.

bearings.paper_claim: The strongest self-report category effects sit at |rho| .08-.14 (abstract p. 843), and the 52 categories explain 5.07 percent of self-report variance (Table 4 p. 854). Effects are typically stronger for longer texts (Table 6 continuous moderators, p. 854).
bearings.paper_location: Abstract p. 843; Table 4 p. 854; Table 6 p. 856
bearings.system_side: Default basis is behavioral (RECEPT_TRAITS default). The lexical fallback is susc = .40A + .30N - .20C - .10E. Shrinkage is min(1, sqrt(tokens/1500)). Code and comments match the rel. The sqrt form is not estimated by this paper.
bearings.transfer_conditions: Closed-vocabulary rates carry little true trait variance, so a lexical composite is mostly noise. This supports keeping the lexical basis out of the default, but not the specific sqrt shrinkage form.
bearings.verifier_note: Code claims match. Softened because the abstract range is .08 to .14, not about .10 to .14 as the rel states, and the paper says nothing about the sqrt shrinkage form.

related.why: Item exists (Measuring Elite Personality Using Speech, 2016). Same closed-vocabulary method applied to congressional speech; the paper sets an effect-size ceiling for that method. Ramey characterization not separately checked.
Item exists. The meta-analysis cites Pennebaker et al. 2003 and LIWC category design rests on this line of work.
Item exists (Predicting the Big 5 from digital footprints, meta-analysis). It is a parallel open-vocabulary meta-analysis. The rel's claim that its effects are larger was not checked in this paper.
Item exists (Personality on the Hill appendix, Senate expert ratings). Observer ratings make the cue-utilization versus cue-validity distinction relevant to reading panel convergence.
Item exists (computational measurement of politicians' agency and communion). Relevant context for the closed-vocabulary ceiling. The claim that it criticizes Ramey-style SVM was not checked here.

Item exists (deep-learning text personality artifact, 2023). This paper does not discuss it, so 'contradicts' is not supported. Relabelled complements: both are benchmark comparisons of text-based trait measurement.
Item exists (The Role of Emotional Stability in Twitter Conversations, 2012). Relevant to the Emotional Stability kernel markers and the affective-N anchor.

summary_issues: Coverage: ext.json and rel.json override files do not exist, so the rel in the item JSON was used. Paul paul_markup is empty and the item has no annotations, so no Paul notes were dropped. All 4110 lines of the text file were searched for the cited numbers and sections; the paper text was not fully read line by line.
Summary says the paper's year is 2022 (correct; received 2022, DOI 10.1037/bul0000381), but the item p.year field still reads 2024 and should be corrected.
Summary LIWC benchmark line '.10 vs .27-.31' omits IBM-WPI at .13, which is above LIWC. It also omits that the LIWC value is a post hoc best-category maximum (Table 7, footnote 9).
Summary ext list says LIWC lags computer methods across the board. Paper text says LIWC beats IBM-WPI for Conscientiousness and Extraversion.

Summary gives Emotional Stability negative emotion as a kernel example. The paper's Emotional Stability kernel marker at |rho| of .10 or more is first-person singular pronouns only, and negative emotion is shown only as a validity effect (-.12). Kernel membership is not shown.

Summary quotes pooled cue-validity figures (|rho| .08-.14, 5.1 percent variance) without the Schwartz 2013 concentration (n = 72,809 of about 84k). Give the with and without Schwartz figures (paper says results almost identical) and state k and n for each figure.
Summary says the brain reads the RKH convergence (CV mean .350, E .510) as method-inflated. Neither figure appears in the brain topic or the fec tree. The brain topic records C +0.348 held-out only.
Summary says the lexical basis is retired from the receptivity layer. Code shows only the default changed; RECEPT_TRAITS=lexical still reverts to it. Reword as a default change.
Ext year-of-publication list omits Conscientiousness swear (validity, b = .006, Table 6). Incomplete, not wrong.
Several rel code line citations were off: SMOreg Agreeableness anger is json line 66, not 43. Bearing 2 cites fec/big5_improvements_eval.py, which does not exist in the repo.

Bearing 2 panel assignments (O academics only, N insiders only, C insider only) and the A-ES .44 and .21 halo figures do not appear in the brain topic, which says only E and A clear both panels and O, C and N are one-panel supported.
